News.title: ‘Alpha male’ boxer killed grandad, 62, with one punch in unprovoked attack & left him for dead as kids watched in horror
News.content:
A FORMER boxer killed a grandad with one punch in an unprovoked attack and left him for dead as kids watched on in horror.

James “Jim” McKeown was found lying on the ground by a member of the public in Beaumont Leys Park, Leicestershire, on April 6.



The 62-year-old had been walking home from a nearby pub when he was viciously assaulted by Joshua Moore, 34, who was riding a quad bike in the park with a young child.

Moore had confronted Mr McKeown and punched him in the face where he fell to the ground and hit his head on the pavement.



He then placed Mr McKeown in the recovery position before fleeing the park without contacting emergency services.

He was raced to Royal Leicester Infirmary but despite the best efforts of medical staff, he died a short time later.



Moore was jailed for five years and nine months after pleading guilty to manslaughter at Leicester Crown Court earlier this month.

CCTV footage released by Leicestershire Police show Moore returning to the scene an hour later telling an officer: “I hit him”.



The force said later how Moore clearly thought “it was more important to sort out his affairs” before calling 999.

They added he went as far as cancelling a tattoo appointment he had booked for the next day.

The court heard how Mr McKeown had been found by a passer-by in a pool of his own blood, reports ITV.

Moore is said to have told cops he had struck Mr McKeown in “self-defence” but this was dismissed by prosecutors.

Sentencing Moore on his 34th birthday, Judge Timothy Spencer told him “there is more than an element of you wanting to be the alpha male”.



He said: “You could simply have ridden on, you could have avoided him, you could have avoided any exchange of words.

“A truly big man would have done just that. But no, you decided to punch him, with these devastating consequences.”

Marie de Redman, defending Moore, said the killer was “truly sorry” for what had happened.



Judge Spencer said that Moore had “never sought to shirk responsibility” but said he was “far too quick with your fists”, labelling Moore’s blows as “powerful and devastating”.

He added that the “attack was committed in the presence of children” and Moore had “simply abandoned” Mr McKeown as he lay unconscious on the ground.

Moore’s previous conviction was also a factor in his sentence after he was jailed for eight years for a burglary in 2016 where he had assaulted another victim.

Following the incident, Mr McKeown’s family paid tribute saying: “We have lost a loving father, brother, partner and grandfather, our lives will never be the same again.

“Jimmy has lived locally for nearly 20 years and was well known in the community, affectionately known to many as Spider,” they added.



Detective Inspector Kevin Hames from East Midlands Special Operations Unit (EMSOU) Murder Investigation Team, said: “Sadly, this is a tragic death that could have been avoided. Moore had a choice that day and should have walked away, without using any violence, Jim posed no threat to him.

“His actions have now left a family devastated at the loss of their loved one.

“The fact that he didn’t make any attempt to contact the emergency services following the incident shows exactly what type of man he is.

“He placed Jim in the recovery position and clearly saw the injuries he had caused but that didn’t stop him from riding away, returning home to organise his affairs before handing himself in.

“Notwithstanding this was a totally unprovoked attack, Joshua Moore should not have been riding a quad bike in the park in the first place.



“While we are pleased that Moore has admitted to being responsible for Jim’s death, there are certainly no winners in the case.

“Jim’s family now face a life without him, and nothing can replace the feeling of that loss. They have shown immense bravery throughout the investigation and subsequent legal proceedings. This has in no way been easy for them.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Moore now faces a lengthy term in prison, and I hope it gives him the opportunity to reflect on his actions.

“I would also like to thank the community of West Leicester for their support in the investigation and thank the members of the community who unlike Joshua Moore, stopped to provide care to Jim.”

News.title: Huge blaze erupts at industrial estate sparking evacuation as plumes of smoke seen for miles
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

'STAY AWAY' Huge blaze erupts at industrial estate sparking evacuation as plumes of smoke seen for miles

A HUGE fire has erupted in the early hours of the morning at an industrial estate, forcing locals to be evacuated from the area.

Firefighters rushed to the scene at Star Trading Estate, Caerleon, Newport at around 2.40am today.



Ten fire engines, an aerial ladder platform and a range of specialist firefighting equipment was used to tackle the inferno.

Pictures show the fire raging, with massive black plumes of smoke rising high into the air.



Fire crews remain at the scene, working to bring the fire under control.

Aerial images reveal the extent of the damage caused by the fire, with the building’s roof caved in and charred surfaces.



In a statement, South Wales Fire and Rescue Service said: “Crews remain in attendance at a large industrial fire at Star Trading Estate, Caerleon, Newport.

“The site has been evacuated, and all persons are accounted for.

“Members of the public are urged to avoid the area to allow emergency services to carry out their work.

“Due to smoke in the vicinity, residents are also advised to keep windows and doors closed.

“SWFRS is working closely with Gwent Police and partner agencies to help ensure public safety. Thank you for your co-operation.”



The cause of the fire has not yet been confirmed and no information has been released regarding any injuries.

Investigations are expected to begin once the fire has been extinguished.

Motorists and residents are advised to avoid the area while firefighting operations continue.

News.title: Boy, 16, killed after scrambler & lorry crash in Tyrone as tributes pour for ‘cheeky’ lad with ‘sparkling blue eyes’
News.content:
ROAD SHOCK Boy, 16, killed after scrambler & lorry crash in Tyrone as tributes pour for ‘cheeky’ lad with ‘sparkling blue eyes’

A 16-YEAR-OLD boy has died following a collision between a scrambler bike and a lorry in Co Tyrone.

The teenage victim has been named as Connor Magee Campbell from the Clonoe area of the county.



The fatal crash occurred in the Derryloughan Road area of Coalisland at around 8.15pm on Thursday.

The teenager was given medical treatment at the scene and rushed to hospital.



However, the PSNI confirmed today that the young lad has since died from his injuries.

Connor is the “beloved son” of Brian and Megan Campbell and the late Kayleigh Magee.



He is also the “much loved brother” of Michael, Daniel and Paudi.

He is also greatly missed by grandparents Mickey and Teresa Campbell, Aileen O’Neill and great grandparents of Kathleen Campbell and Mickey O’Neill.

He is predeceased by his late grandfather Christopher Magee.

No funeral arrangements have been confirmed but the family have requested the house remain private until young Connor’s wake.



Connor’s school has led tributes to him this morning as news of his shock passing spreads through the local area.

St Joseph’s College in Coalisland said: “It is with profound sadness that the St Joseph’s College, Coalisland community has learned of the passing of our former pupil, Connor Magee, following a road traffic accident.

“Connor had recently completed his final year at the College and was looking forward to receiving his GCSE results. He remained a much-loved member of our school community, and his loss is deeply felt by students, staff and all who knew him.”

Tributes have also poured in from the wider community today as they grieve the loss of the teenager.

One person added to the school’s tribute: “Was a pleasure to be part of your journey in St Joseph’s a great lad with the best sense of fun. Rest in Peace Connor.”



Another person wrote: “I am so so sorry to hear this news, such a lovely lad.”

A third said: “Such a lovely lad taken far too soon who will be sorely missed.”

Frank Gervin Clonoe ABC, a boxing club in the area, also paid tribute to Connor who was a longtime member.

Conor’s parents previously coached at the club, adding another layer of heartbreak for the group.

They penned: “It is with great sadness that we learn of the passing of our member, Connor Magee Campbell.



“Connor was a bright, cheeky and lively young lad whose sparkling blue eyes and infectious personality brought joy to those around him.

“He will be fondly remembered by everyone who had the privilege of knowing him through our club and beyond.”

Following the crash on Thursday the PSNI have appealed for witnesses to come forward.

In a statement today Detective Inspector Stewart from the Police Service’s Collision Investigation Unit said: “We received a report at approximately 8.15pm on Thursday evening, 30th July of a collision involving a scrambler and Scania lorry in the Derryloughan Road area.

“Officers attended, alongside Northern Ireland Ambulance Service colleagues – and medical treatment was provided at the scene.



“The 16-year-old, who has been named as Connor Magee Campbell from the Clonoe area, was taken onward to hospital where he sadly later died from his injuries.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We would like to hear from witnesses or anyone who may have captured dash-cam or other footage of what happened, which could assist with our ongoing enquiries.

“Please call us on 101, quoting reference number 1724 30/07/26, or submit information online at https://reporting.psni.police.uk/appeals.”

News.title: Vile rapist who attacked four women including girl, 15, to ‘teach them a lesson for being out at night’ could walk free
News.content:
FREEDOM BID Vile rapist who attacked four women including girl, 15, to ‘teach them a lesson for being out at night’ could walk free

A VILE rapist who targeted four women including a 15-year-old girl to “teach her a lesson” for being out late at night could walk free from prison next month.

Sunny Islam was handed an indefinite sentence in 2012 after launching a three-month reign of terror across east London.

Armed with a knife and plastic cable ties, he dragged his victims off the street, bound them, and subjected them to brutal sexual assaults.

Police fear he may have attacked many more who have never come forward.





Now, it has emerged that Islam could be released in September following a upcoming parole hearing, according to Parole Board documents.

Despite an application from one of his victims to hold the proceedings in public, the Parole Board has ruled it will take place behind closed doors -partly because the prospect of facing the public gave the rapist “anxiety”.

New documents reveal that Islam’s solicitor claimed his health had suffered after hearing of the public application, warning it could impact his ability to give “best evidence”.

His solicitor said: “Since learning that an application has been made for the oral hearing to be held in public, the prisoner has reported a dramatic increase in his anxiety, including sleep disturbance.

“This could be a potentially de-stabilising effect. He is in the process of seeking medical advice in relation to those difficulties; however, at this

stage, no documentary medical evidence is available due to the short space of time elapsed.

“While this factor is not relied upon as determinative, it is relevant

to the Board’s assessment of the likely impact of a public hearing on [the

prisoner’s] ability to participate effectively and give his best evidence.”

No medical documentation was provided to support the claim but Judge Jeremy Roberts denied the victim’s request, citing Islam’s “anxiety” and noting that a public hearing might cause distress to the other victims, whose views were unknown.

The judge added that the applicant could still request to attend the private hearing or receive a summary of the final decision.



Islam, who grew up in a strict Muslim family and told his trial jury he was a practising believer, was 21 when he carried out the attacks in 2010.

He was eventually sentenced to a minimum term of 11 years, which expired in 2021 taking into account time served – convicted of seven counts of rape, one of sexual assault, and one of kidnap, leading to his indefinite imprisonment.

Detectives finally caught the vile rapist after he kidnapped and twice raped a 15-year-old girl in September 2010.

She begged the sick fiend for mercy, telling him she was only 11 years old, but he drove her to a secluded spot and carried out the attack anyway.

In a victim impact statement read to the court back in 2012, the then teenager said: “No one will ever understand the flashbacks, they are so real, at night I lay in my bed and it is like I am there.



“It is like a screen in my mind forcing me to relive that night again and again. People will say time will heal, but I think time has helped me accept the truth — that I will never escape what happened.”

Judge Lees said at the time: “You told her you were going to ‘teach her a lesson’.

“Those words are a chilling indictment of your very troubling attitude towards all of these victims.

“You seem to observe women out at night as not deserving respect or protection.”

Tracing the car’s number plate led police to Islam’s home in Barking, where DNA evidence linked him to three other horrific assaults.



Woolwich Crown Court heard how he subjected a 20-year-old sex worker to “his trademark double rape” in July 2010, tying her up and punching her repeatedly when she fought back.

Just a week later, Islam struck in Forest Gate, dragging a 28-year-old woman into his car and forcing her to commit a sex act.

She bravely kicked out the back window and tried to flag down passing drivers while Islam strangled her, eventually breaking free to rejoin her friends, who called the police.

His final victim, a 31-year-old woman attacked that September, only came to light after officers discovered her blood in the back of the vehicle alongside his knife and cable ties.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She had been beaten until she bled, bound, and twice raped.



The Sun have contacted the Parole Board for comment.

News.title: F-35 fighter jet crashes at Top Gun Navy training base sparking fire after ‘aircraft mishap’ as pilot rushed to hospital
News.content:
A FIGHTER jet crashed at a US Navy training base where the iconic Top Gun movie was filmed as the horror smash sparked a huge fire.

The single-seat F-35B Lightning II aircraft plummeted to the ground just off the runway at Marine Corps Air Station Miramar in California, at around 10am on Friday.



Footage showed huge plumes of thick smoke billowing from the crash site as firefighters douse the flames.

The wreckage was surrounded by blackened ground after the crash triggered a grass fire that ripped through the field.



“F-35 short final crash,” the Miramar air traffic control tower told firefighters in audio recorded by LiveATC.net.

“It appeared that the parachute did deploy … and a pilot ejected.”

A spokesman for the Marine Corps base said the dramatic crash was caused by an “aviation mishap”.

“The pilot ejected and has been recovered”, he added.

Emergency crews rushed the pilot to hospital and he was admitted “in stable condition”.

The cause of the crash was not immediately clear.



Billed as “the most advanced jet fighter in the world” by its manufacturer, the $102million F-35B is a stealth aircraft.

It can land like a conventional plane and vertically, like a helicopter.

The more than 50-foot-long jet is operated by the US Marines, the United Kingdom and the Italian Air Force.



MCAS Miramar is known around the world as the one-time home of the US Navy’s “Top Gun” school for elite pilots.

The training ground was featured in the 1986 hit Top Gun starring Tom Cruise.

About 15,000 service members from all branches of the military are based at the San Diego camp.

It comes as a NATO fighter jet burst into flames mid-air and crash- landed in Greece.

Shocking footage showed the burning Hellenic Air Force F-16 being doused in water after touching down in Zante.



It is currently unclear what caused the Nato plane to burn mid-air.

There is speculation that the aircraft had a problem with its landing gear as it touched down.

The plane belongs to the 116th Combat Wing and had taken off from the Araxos Air Base, in Peloponnese.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The pilot is said to have escaped without any major injuries, according to local media.

Emergency services immediately hosed down the plane with foam and water after it skidded onto the tarmac.

News.title: The insiders dismantling Putin’s iron grip from within as Russia’s ruling elite turn on tyrant in humiliating blow
News.content:
VLADIMIR Putin’s ruling elite are growing “increasingly impatient” with the Kremlin leader as his dictatorship edges closer to collapse, insiders told The Sun.

Those closest to Putin are moving their money abroad as they break rank to prepare for a coming “mutiny” and a new Russia.



Russia’s top banker German Gref, 62, exposed the growing divide between Putin and the Russian elite when he demanded the dictator end his faltering war in Ukraine.

The former member of Putin’s top team accused the tyrant of tanking the economy to avoid a humiliating peace deal.



Weeks later another Putin-loyal oligarch, Andrey Melnichenko, made a public plea to the West.

The fertiliser kingpin called for economic support and an end to Putin’s one-man rule.



It is unprecedented for a prominent Russian official to publicly make demands of Putin.

Ukraine has spent weeks blitzing oil depots with state-of-the-art drones, before shifting its crosshairs to a series of strikes that have crippled the regime’s biggest e-commerce platform.



The attacks have tanked Russia’s already reeling economy – wiping out businesses, suffocating trade and sparking nationwide fuel shortages.

Russia’s elites are driven by their financial interests and “self-preservation”, Ukraine War Analyst Jason Smart told The Sun.

He added: “They understand that Putin’s regime is on very shaky ground. And at this point, there’s a very good chance that it will fall.”

In the last year, Russia’s richest people have been quietly moving billions of dollars abroad, according to reports.

The outflow of capital from Russia is estimated to be in the tens of billions of dollars so far.



Jason said this is a sign that cohesion within the Kremlin is breaking.

He said: “They are doing what they can right now to make sure that they are able to preserve their assets.”

Putin’s public appearances have fallen dramatically in recent months.



A fresh ring of steel has been thrown up around the Valdai fortress -the tyrant’s main home during the war – and it’s now encircled by 27 modern air defence system emplacements.

And Russia’s national guard has been bolstered in numbers and firepower – including tank units.

The 400,000-strong force reports directly to Putin — bypassing the Russian Ministry.

Jason said: “Why do you need tanks unless you’re gonna have battle with other tanks?

“But that’s exactly what they’re planning for. The potential for mutiny.



“There are those around Putin who understand that his days are numbered.”

The Putin regime is made of “different clans working together in the same system under Putin”, Jason said.

But with Putin out of the picture, they will be left to divide up the wealth of Russia.



Jason said: “At this point it’s a question, not just of the future of Putin, but the future of Russia. That also means there’s a high chance for violence.

“These different groups – who have been able to patch together for a number of years – don’t feel there’s much allegiance between them.

“Instead their long-standing feuds, their hatred for each other, is boiling to the surface.

“Those that are the losers will lose everything.”

And it’s not just those at home turning on Putin, as his international allies withdraw from the dictator on multiple fronts.



Russian dissident Igor Eidman told The Sun: “The Kremlin elites are growing impatient.

“They understand the war cannot be won and are increasingly promoting the idea that something has to change, and urgently.

“The leaders of Kazakhstan and the Central Asian states maintain close ties with the Russian oligarchic elite, and will side with their view.”



Last week Putin was left squirming when his long time ally, the President of Kazakhstan, publicly told him to “freeze” the war in Ukraine.

Kassym-Jomart Tokayev said the “point” of the conflict was no longer clear, during a meeting in Omsk, Russia.

He said: “Perhaps it is already time to freeze this conflict return to the Istanbul 2.0 formula, as significant results were achieved there.

“After that – naturally under guarantees from major powers, including Russia – we can move forward.”

Tokayev was referring to the negotiations held between Russia and Ukraine in Turkey last year.



John Foreman CBE, former UK Defence Attaché to Russia, told The Sun Tokayev’s bold statement was likely a warning to Putin that he will “not be pushed around”.

The leader of Kazakhstan could also be signalling to his own international allies that he has “not picked a side”, and is “open for business”.

Last week, Ukraine struck an oil terminal on the Black Sea forcing Kazakhstan’s main oil terminal to close.

One source said the devastating blitz caused its biggest oil field to slash output by more than half.

“The war is destabilising relations and harming everyone including Kazakhstan,” Foreman said.



Putin did not respond to his ally’s appeal, but it came the very same week that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said a “ceasefire” would be “better” than a prolonged war.

Russia has suffered 1.4 million casualties including 500,000 deaths since invading Ukraine in 2022.

A report last month showed that the average life expectancy for Russian troops on the frontline was just 20 minutes.



And now, the Kremlin is reportedly preparing for another mass mobilisation to prolong Putin’s meatgrinder war.

Tokayev joins a stream of Russian allies openly condemning the war in Ukraine, as the scale of Putin’s disaster continues to unfold.

“The world has turned following Putin’s self-inflicted strategic catastrophe in 2022,” Foreman said.

“A ferocious Ukraine on his borders, huge casualties, a bigger NATO, Russia’s former territories in Central Asia distancing themselves, and China taking Russia to the cleaners.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Now, leaders in Armenia, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan are all hedging away from Moscow.



And the restructure has left space for China and the US in a traditionally Russian sphere of influence, Foreman said.

News.title: Moment husband who stabbed his wife 40 times because she wanted a divorce lies to cops saying ‘she attacked me’
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a man who stabbed his wife 40 times after she asked for a divorce lies to police, saying “she attacked me.”

Syed Rafay Ahmad, 45, attacked his wife Anam, 36, with a kitchen knife in their home in Wythenshawe, Manchester, on January 27.



After the brutal knife attack, Ahmad sent a message to his family WhatsApp group and to Anam’s dad saying: “I have killed my wife.”

Video footage of the moment Ahmad was arrested shows him walking down a flight of stairs in his flat.



Officers at the bottom of the stairs can be heard shouting at him, telling him to put his hands in the air.

Ahmad complies and walks down the stairs, hands in the air to the officers before being ordered to turn and put his hands behind his back.



Once officers have him in handcuffs he is marched outside to a waiting police car.

Police put him under caution for suspicion of a section 18 assault before placing him in the car.



As the arresting officer finishes speaking Ahmad interrupts and starts saying: “Self defence, self defence.”

The cop shouts over him and demands to know if “that [his rights] all makes sense.”

Ahmad says he understands before trying again to lie his way out of cuffs – saying: “She was attacking me.”

The police officer interrupts Ahmad and warns him to be quiet, saying: “You’re under caution, so don’t say anything.”

Ahmad apologises before he is searched a final time and placed into the back of a police vehicle.



While searching the killer, cops ask him where the knife is and Ahmad calmly says: “Inside, kitchen I think.”

Ahmad was initially arrested on suspicion of assault but despite the best efforts of paramedics, his wife was pronounced dead at the scene.

She had suffered 40 stab wounds in the savage attack.



Ahmad pleaded guilty to murder during a trial this week at Manchester Crown Court.

He has now been sentenced to life in prison with a minimum term of 27 years.

Detective Inspector Neil Higginson from our Major Incident Team said: “My thoughts, firstly, remain with Anam’s family and loved ones, who suffered an unimaginable loss as a result of Ahmad’s actions.

“Anam’s tragic death was a result of Ahmad’s violent nature. This was a horrific, and cold-blooded attack, causing irreparable damage to a family, who were left to deal with the consequences of his actions.

“The sentencing passed today will ensure we keep a violent offender behind bars for a long time.



“I would like to thank the victim’s family who have supported this investigation, and their strength throughout what is no doubt an incredibly difficult time, is no small feat.

“I would also like to thank all the members of the public who came forward to report to us and supported the victim at the time of the incident.

News.title: 'I moved to France for a taste of Paradise but woke up in an apocalypse'
News.content:
For the past 10 days, I’ve been perilously close to the wildfires of the Gironde - and witnessed my first and France’s first fire cloud. I love France, and the prospect of long, sunny summer days, mild winters, and a gentler pace of life ticked all my boxes when, having worked hard and raised a daughter, I moved here in 2021, with Bordeaux on my doorstep. But I'd never bargained for the extremes of weather.

In June of 2022, I found myself in the eye of a tornado. My house is on a hill, with panoramic views, which is great. But that afternoon winds of 140km/hour battered my house. I had a friend staying. Thank god. Between us we battled against a horizontal sheet of rain that chewed up the garden, blew in and buckled my French doors, and tore tiles off the roof. Total cost of damage 12,000 euros.

Another almighty storm in 2023, again in June, wrought havoc in my commune, destroying vines, bringing down trees. Then came 2024, a year marked by floods. Months and months of rain and more rain saw the banks of several rivers burst, flooding towns, villages, and fields. Now, with the wild fires, it’s crazy. The stats are staggering: 220,000 people evacuated from the Gironde and Landes - the biggest evacuation of people in France since the second world war; 300,000 hectares across Spain and France scorched. And no official assessment of the animals lost.

Whitney Houston fans set to splash cash as star's prized items hit auction block READ MORE :

View 4 Images A startled fox watches as woodland burns (Image: Supplied)

‌



France’s minister for Ecological Transition, Monique Barbut, stated that the damage to wildlife in the region would be catastrophic, with significant losses among birds, deer and amphibians. Entire groups of deer have been photographed trapped at the forest's edge. One wildlife officer speaking about areas such as Le Porge, said: “Nothing can survive. The fires came too early, at the height of the breeding season. Birds were nesting, fawns lay hidden in the undergrowth.”

Equally staggering has been the response of the people. Across the nation, we’ve all come together to supply food, clothing and shelter to the victims. Animal rescue centres are co-ordinating their efforts and gathering food, bedding, and medication for lost and wounded animals. Jane Marple, animal rescue veteran and head of a local animal association, told me: “This morning a new part of the inner evacuation zone opened for rescuers. This part of the fire zone has been closed since the fires started. We now have night goggles, as we know many animals will lay low during the day and move in the night.”

My friend and I took animal food to St Thomas de Conac – a small village on the Estuary – where we met Mary with her van half-packed, ready to drive up to Ile d’Oleron. We’ve been told to avoid Bordeaux and head north with provisions. Everyone is pitching in “Bordeaux, we’re coming,” read a post on social media, as a convoy of tractors carrying water tanks joined a motorway into the city. Heading across from the Dordogne came a fleet of ambulances to help with the evacuations.

View 4 Images Karen and Mary loads up animal supplies (Image: Supplied)

‌



Such displays of solidarity and comradeship make me incredibly proud to live in this country that I call home. We are all in this together - well, apart from a few ‘ex-pats’ who have complained that their swimming pools have been damaged by falling ash. Yes, really! I do have some sympathy for those gite owners who have lost bookings. The whole of France is not ablaze. It’s a big country. The advice has only ever been to stay away from the Gironde and do not head south via the A63 into Spain, which is battling its own megafire hell.

If the fires had started 20km north of Bordeaux instead of West, I wouldn’t be writing this. I’d be in an evacuation centre, just like the parc d’exposition, grateful for clothes, food, water – grateful to the firefighters working tirelessly to save lives. Friends of mine who live in Merignac, beside the airport, were evacuated and are still not home. Some German friends are still in the parc d’expostion, waiting to return to their holiday home to collect their belongings. Many of the evacuees were holidaymakers and tourists, but many locals have lost their houses, their pets, their livelihoods.

I live about 30 minutes north of Bordeaux – in the shadow of the megafires. I watched from my back porch as the firecloud headed this way. A fire cloud, or pyrocumulonimbus, happens when a wildfire is so intense it built its own thunderstorm. The cloud creates its own lightning, hurls embers up to 30 km ahead of the fire front, and drives the flames in directions no one can predict.

View 4 Images The dramatic view from Linda's porch (Image: Supplied)

‌



Last Friday, smoke from the Cap Ferat and Biscarosse fires travelled up the Gironde estuary and choked my neighbourhood. The ominous black cloud sat above us for almost 12 hours, dispensing no rain, just bangs and flashes from the thunder and lightning. At 9 o’clock on Saturday morning my neighbours and I were transfixed by the eerie silence that followed. No birds, no wind, just an end-of-the-world glow coming from the south.

As I write, the fires are stable but the smell of smoke still lingers in the air. We suffered temperatures of 42C again yesterday. This is our third big canicule (a period of scorching heat) this year, and each time they last for days or weeks… And still no rain in my commune. My fruit trees have died. All around me, fields of maize and sunflowers are stunted. The grapes are splitting on the vines. Walking in forests is prohibited, so is hunting (no bad thing!).

The French aren’t good with rules. If we see one we like to bend it or break it, but along with the camaraderie I’ve witnessed has come a new respect for nature and the environment. We’ve just received a stark reminder of how fragile it all is. And we are working together to protect it.,My adopted home of south-west France is beautiful, wild and charming – and a million miles away from my former life in London – but I wouldn’t go back no matter what the weather decides to fling at me.

News.title: Prince William warning on Harry's UK return - with fresh battle on horizon
News.content:
Prince William warning on Harry's UK return - with fresh battle on horizon

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's recent reunion with King Charles is said to have left them buoyed into believing they can rekindle their relationship with the royal family - and reverse Megxit

View 6 Images Prince William and Prince Harry (Image: Martin Meissner/AP/REX/Shutterstock)

King Charles may be welcoming Prince Harry back with open arms, but the same can't be said for his estranged brother Prince William.

‌



After years of tensions between Harry, Meghan Markle, and the rest of the royal family, the Sussexes spent time with King Charles at his Highgrove home on 10 July. It was the first time the monardch had been able to see his grandchildren, Archie and Lilibet, in person, since 2022.

‌



But the reunion reportedly came with a caveat that details were to remain strictly private. It was perhaps something of a litmus test for Harry, who has famously criticised his family on a number of occasions - to Oprah, in the couple's Netflix show, and - in unflinching detail - in Spare. As such, trust is a major issue when it comes to the Sussexes.

‌



Prince Harry gives definitive list of his occupations in chaotic Joe Marler interview READ MORE :

View 6 Images Harry and Meghan recently reunited with King Charles at his Highgrove home

While Buckingham Palace confirmed in a brief statement that the meeting had taken place, an aide said no further details or pictures would be released. And so far there has been no word from Harry about the meeting.

But it has raised questions about the Sussexes' motives for returning to the UK. Harry has long said that he was unable to bring his wife and children back to Britain because of the threat to his security. He lost an appeal over the dismissal of his High Court claim against the Home Office last year after the Royal and VIP Executive Committee (Ravec), which decides on the security provision for senior royals, decided he should receive a reduced degree of security protection.

‌



Ahead of his return to the UK earlier this month, a report was submitted - commissioned by Harry's own private security firm - detailing dozens of threats and potential attacks. His team had put in a formal request for police security while he was in the UK - but they were again told that no taxpayer-funded security would be provided.

View 6 Images William has shown no desire to reconnect with his estranged brother Harry (Image: Getty Images)

Recent reports suggest, however, that after the meeting with his father, Harry is hopeful for more family reunions - and will therefore continue in his bid for taxpayer-funded security. It remains to be seen whether he will ever get the protection he insists he needs.

‌



On the security row, royal historian Marlene Koenig tells the Mirror: "They have proven that nothing happened during this stay – their private events at Highgrove and Althorp escaped the cameras, which proves they can visit with only their security."

So what of Harry's desire to reconcile with the royals? Could it be simply a son hoping to spend time with his ageing father, who has been fighting cancer since February 2024? Charles would no doubt have been delighted to see his young grandchildren given the infrequency of their visits to the UK.

View 6 Images Charles welcomed Harry and his family back to the UK for a visit (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"The primary purpose of the visit, which was about 90 minutes to two hours long, was for Charles to spend time with his grandkids," Marlene tells us. "Tea, a walk through the gardens, Harry showing and telling Archie and Lilibet about his childhood – the pool, the treehouse, with far less emphasis on serious conversation between father and son."

If it does pave the way for more meetings between the Sussexes and the monarch, questions will be raised over their positions and roles moving forward. It's been suggested that Harry and Meghan are still seeking out some form of 'half-in, half-out' arrangement - something the late Queen expressly forbade. Essentially, the couple want to carry on making money in the US and elsewhere to fund their lifestyle in Montecito, but to be treated as 'working royals' when in the UK while doing charity work and public events.

Mystery remains over whether this set-up could really work long-term. Prince William will one day take the throne - and he has made no secret of his desire to slim down the monarchy. Certainly it seems there will be no place for Harry or Meghan.

‌



View 6 Images William and Harry have not spoken for years, it's understood

William is known to take a much harder line than Charles, and while he was said to be supportive of his father's decision to see the Sussexes this month, his stance on them has not changed.

Sources say neither he nor Princess Kate had any desire to meet with Harry and Meghan - and the once close bond the brothers shared looks irreparably shattered.

‌



Could it be that Harry is looking to cement his position before his brother takes power? And will that be enough? Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor was famously stripped of all his titles by his brother - the only thing Charles could not unilaterally remove was Andrew's place in the line of succession, which remains at eighth in line.

View 6 Images The brothers' bond has been broken (Image: (Image: Getty))

As one source close to Harry and Meghan told the Mail: "Everyone knows their future is not in his dad's hands – it's in his brother's."

Article continues below

Nevertheless, the Sussexes are said to be determined to reverse Megxit, and are contemplating using their holiday home in Portugal as a staging post back to Britain. The paper reports: "This is coming from Meghan as well as from him... she is fully behind it."

But another source suggested there might be an altogether different motive for Harry's desire to reconnect with his royal roots: "I don't think he's ever wanted to be estranged from his family. I think when he was madly in love with Meghan he could be blind enough to choose her. Now things are different, and the veil is lifting."

Certainly Harry has been vocal in the past about his hopes of reconciling with his family. During an interview with the BBC last year, he said: "Of course, some members of my family will never forgive me for writing a book, of course, they will never forgive me for lots of things, but I would love reconciliation with my family. There's no point in continuing to fight anymore."

News.title: Marco Pierre White blasts 'fake' MasterChef over cold food and reveals how stock cubes changed his life
News.content:
When it comes to cooking, Marco Pierre White certainly knows his onions and he has little appetite for shows like MasterChef.

In fact, the knives are out, as the ‘enfant terrible’ of haute cuisine declares: “Number one it is a reality show. Number two, when it comes to the tasting the food is three, four hours old. It's cold food. It is a TV show, don't take it seriously. It is not real. It is fantasy. If it makes you want to cook then that is all that matters. It’s food porn."

Britain’s first celebrity chef, Marco - who is included in a new paperback book Blood, Sweat and Asparagus Spears: The Story of the 1990s Restaurant Revolution by Andrew Turvil - is preparing to star in a new three-part BBC series later this year, called The Rise of the Rockstar Chef.

Set against the ‘Cool Britannia’ backdrop of the nineties, it will chart his colourful career, also featuring Gordon Ramsay, his apprentice, and Heston Blumenthal.

‌



Whitney Houston fans set to splash cash as star's prized items hit auction block READ MORE :

5 View 5 Images He is preparing to star in a new three-part BBC series, The Rise of the Rockstar Chef (Image: ITV) 5 View 5 Images Chefs Jean Christophe Novelli, Marco and Gordon Ramsay seen together in the year 2000 (Image: Richard Young/Shutterstock)

A frequent guest judge on MasterChef Australia, Marco reaches boiling point, as he recalls: "I remember when I was on I looked at the plate, and I don't like to criticise, so I said ‘that little bit is so nice’.”

Claiming he was less than truthful, he adds: “I had to go and see my priest afterwards.”

‌



This is just a taste of the kind of explosive anecdotes viewers can expect on the new show, which will delve into the friendships, fights and feuds that characterised the three chefs’ rise to fame.

Meanwhile, Marco's return to the spotlight will mark nearly 40 years since he opened his first restaurant, Harveys, on Wandsworth Common, London, in 1987 - earning him his first Michelin star almost immediately, and his second a year later.

Injecting an explosion of flavour into the British restaurant scene, with his ingredient led simplicity, Marco arrived in London with just £7.36, a box of books and a bag of clothes.

But his classical training as a commis chef with Albert and Michel Roux at the two-Michelin starred La Gavroche made him a champion.

‌



Freely admitting he learned from the best - with mentors also including Raymond Blanc, Pierre Koffmann and the late chef Nico Ladenis, before becoming an assistant at the Six Bells pub on Chelsea’s famous King’s Road, under American chef Mario Batali.

After six years running Harveys, where Marco first met Gordon Ramsay, he became chef-patron of The Restaurant Marco Pierre White at the Hyde Park Hotel. There, he became the youngest chef to achieve three Michelin stars, before moving to the Oak Room at London’s Le Meridien Piccadilly Hotel.

Then, after a 17 year pursuit of culinary perfection, Marco shocked the world of gastronomy in 1999 by turning his back on his career and returning his Michelin stars.

View 5 Images Bradley Cooper in the 2015 film Burnt (Image: Publicity Picture)

‌



Twenty seven years later, he has no regrets. Of Michelin stars, he says: "They [Michelin] know more about tyres than they do about food. Today, I go to Michelin starred restaurants and they confuse me. If you go to a two star or a three star you are told what you are eating. The romance has gone. In my opinion, they have turned gastronomy into a canapé party.”

Marco also believes there is too little discipline and an excess of drink and drugs in kitchens. He says: "I did not start drinking alcohol until I was 41. I have never taken a drug in my life. Today, there's drugs and drink. I don't think it is in the world of gastronomy [fine dining] but I think it is everywhere. It is pretty sad, the reality of this.”

Marco also says Gordon Ramsay’s expletive filled rants are tame, compared to his own early experiences in kitchens. He says: "If I think what my head chef used to call me...that is another conversation. But you know, a good b*****king did not do anybody any harm. It gave me backbone. It gave me a spine. In that world you were never late, you never called in sick and you would learn. Today, people call in sick and people look at their watch. I was knocked down and had things thrown at me! I am glad I was b*****ked."

Marco’’s famous temper flares when he is compared to Carmen "Carmy" Berzatto, played by Jeremy Allen White, in the American TV drama The Bear; or Bradley Cooper in the 2015 film Burnt.

‌



View 5 Images Marco with his brothers and father's greyhound (Image: ExpressStar)

He says: "Let me tell you, The Bear and The Burnt is fluff. Don't believe it. It is way worse!”

Asked by now disgraced Harvey Weinstein to coach Bradley Cooper for the part, Marco refused. He says: "It is manufactured drama.”

While he no longer cooks professionally, Marco remains forthright with his opinions about cuisine.

‌



And, when it comes to flavour, he has a surprising secret weapon. He says: "Knorr stock cubes are life changing. If it had not been for Knorr I would not have won three stars in Michelin. Whenever I cook something, I always use a little bit of Knorr instead of stock.

"Why? When I was a boy of 17 I was told ‘it does not matter how you create the desired effect, as long as you create the desired effect’.

"My customers don't care whether it is salt or Knorr as long as it tastes delicious.”

The Rise of the Rockstar Chef airs on BBC1 later this year. Blood, Sweat and Asparagus Spears by Andrew Turvil is out now priced £10.99 by Elliott & Thompson

News.title: 'I hate my £8k Love Island face transformation - family don't even recognise me'
News.content:
'I hate my £8k Love Island face transformation - family don't even recognise me'

EXCLUSIVE: Jess Pendrey took inspiration from former Love Island contestants as a teenager, purchasing her first ever cosmetic procedure as soon as she turned 18-years-old before it spiralled out of control

View 10 Images

A young woman who looks practically unrecognisable from her teen years has shared a heartbreaking warning to others after getting addicted to cosmetic procedures.

‌



When Jess Pendrey turned 18, there wasn't one feature she particularly disliked about herself. But within months, she had booked her first lip filler appointment - a decision that sparked years of cosmetic work, thousands of pounds of spending and an endless pursuit of the next treatment she believed would make her happier.

‌



Now 21, the Brighton bartender says she barely recognises the person staring back at her in old photographs. Now she's preparing to have all of her her lip filler dissolved as she embraces a more natural look, after taking inspiration from Love Island contestants for years.

‌



Humiliated bride left stranded at altar without a wheelchair ramp to reach her husband READ MORE :

View 10 Images Jess Pendrey

Over the next three years, Jess underwent a long list of cosmetic procedures, including lip filler, chin filler, jaw filler, cheek filler, nose filler, masseter Botox, composite bonding in Turkey, a £4,500 breast augmentation and non-surgical body contouring treatments.

In total, she estimates she has spent around £8,000. Working as a waitress at the time, Jess says virtually every spare penny she earned went towards funding her next appointment.

‌



"I was never happy," she reveals. "I was always waiting for the next thing. I was spending all my money. All my wages were going on these appointments."

10 View 10 Images Jess has always wanted to model but found it hard after altering her face with procedures 10 View 10 Images Jess has spent thousands on procedures

‌



While nobody in her family or friendship group encouraged the procedures, Jess says social media constantly did. Her mother strongly opposed every treatment, but Jess often booked appointments without telling her.

"My mum hated everything I had done, ever, but I just kept going back for top-ups," she says. "It was so easy. You can see something online, book it the day before and completely change your face."

Jess says she became fixated on the polished aesthetic promoted by influencers and former Love Island contestants, particularly Lucinda Strafford, whose glamorous appearance she desperately wanted to emulate.

‌



10 View 10 Images Lucinda Strafford served as inspiration for Jess who wanted to look more like her (Image: Getty Images for the NTA's) 10 View 10 Images Jess now looks unrecognisable compared to her teenage self

"Lucinda was a big one when I was 18 or 19," she explains. "Looking back now, she's a very pretty girl, but she's her. She's obviously spent money on what she looks like. But that's not me."

‌



Rather than boosting her confidence, Jess says each procedure simply fuelled the desire for another and it became a vicious cyle. "Every part of my body I could touch, I did," she says. "Everything became a competition. I'd follow a new girl and then I'd want whatever she'd had done."

She describes scrolling through social media feeds packed with before-and-after videos, clinic promotions and discounted treatment packages that made cosmetic procedures feel both normal and irresistible.

"You see exactly what they've had done and how they've managed to look a certain way," she explains. "Every day you're seeing a new offer. There are packages on offer. I even bought a 4ml tweak package where they did my nose, jaw and cheeks all in one day. I went straight back to work afterwards."

‌



10 View 10 Images Jess has now started modelling and is working to reverse some of the procedures she has had done 10 View 10 Images The first treatment Jess had done was lip filler aged 18

Jess believes social media often presents an unrealistic standard of beauty, with influencers showcasing heavily edited images that bear little resemblance to reality. "Creators post the best photos of themselves," she says. "That's not what they actually look like. No-one is perfect."

‌



Her obsession with appearance soon extended beyond social media. Even on nights out, Jess says she constantly compared herself with other women. "I would look around the room and fixate on what everyone else looked like," she admits. "The only thing I thought I had going for me was the way I looked."

She received cruel criticism online for the amount of cosmetic work she had done, and the experience really opened her eyes to the cruelty of anonymous social media users.

"I'm lucky that I don't really care what people say, because if I'd been in a bad place it could have really affected me. But I was shocked by how people were hating on me for getting work done. Anyone who commented something bad was on a private account."

‌



10 View 10 Images Jess is now hoping to pursue modelling 10 View 10 Images Jess admitted she's received online hate for her cosmetic procedures

Now, Jess is taking steps to reverse some of the changes she made. She is due to have her lip filler dissolved and says pursuing modelling has also encouraged her to appreciate the features she was once trying to erase. To get filler dissolved, sessions can range from £150 to £300 per area. The procedure uses an injected enzyme called hyaluronidase to safely break down hyaluronic acid-based fillers.

‌



However if filler has migrated, it can cost thousands to reach more complex areas and can be painful, with some describing intense burning sensations as the solution spreads through the tissue.

"I'm building up my modelling portfolio now, and they actually love unique faces," she says. "I miss what I used to look like. I look like a completely different person. People don't even recognise me anymore, and that really stressed me out."

Although she doesn't regret her decisions, as she believes they have helped her grow, Jess hopes other young women think carefully before following beauty trends online.

Article continues below

"It didn't make me feel any better," she says. "I think everything happens for a reason, and I was always going to try it. But I don't even really look at social media anymore because it's so toxic."

News.title: A Place In The Sun's Laura Hamilton relives horror of watching teen die on beach
News.content:
As a presenter on TV’s A Place in the Sun, Laura Hamilton is used to filming happy couples on wave-washed sands. But after witnessing a horrifying beach tragedy she is now determined to use her voice to help save the lives of others.

The 44-year-old mum of two has thrown her support behind the Mirror’s Save Lives for Sam water safety campaign in a bid to end the shocking number of children who drown each year in England.

Laura explains: “How could I not back this campaign? This issue is so important and my recent experience simply reinforced the fact we have to get the water safety message out there.” Laura, who lives in Surrey, was filming in Montpellier in the south of France earlier this month for the hit Channel 4 property show when she witnessed the reality of the dangers of open water.

Roman Kemp clears up hilarious misunderstanding about his famous parents READ MORE :

View 4 Images After witnessing a horrifying beach tragedy she is now determined to use her voice to help save the lives of others (Image: Instagram/ @laurahamiltontv)

‌



The presenter, who has been on screen with A Place in the Sun since 2012, remembers: “We had finished filming for the day a few hours earlier than expected so I thought I’d jump in the car and head to the beach - it wasn’t far away.

“But when I got there I saw a lot of commotion. There was a helicopter landing, an ambulance - all the emergency services. I didn’t know what was happening at first.

“Then I realised someone had been in difficulty in the water. There was an attempt going on to resuscitate the person and they put sheets up so people couldn’t see. In the end they didn’t manage it. I watched it unfold around me. It was shocking and horrible. I later found out it was a 19-year-old lad who had lost his life. I just can’t imagine what that boy’s family is going through. As a mum it struck me - I have a son myself.”

She admits the incident had a profound effect on her: “I didn't sleep very well that night because I just kept playing over and over what I’d seen. My mind was racing. Obviously we don’t know exactly what happened, although there are very strong undercurrents in that area, and I hesitated in talking about it publicly because it’s sensitive - someone has lost their life.

‌



“But for me it just reinforced the fact that getting the message about water safety out there is crucial. That’s why I’m backing the Mirror campaign.”

View 4 Images Laura lives in Surrey with son Rocco, 12 and 11-year-old daughter Tahlia (Image: Instagram)

Save Lives for Sam is calling for urgent action to stop the huge number of children who lose their lives through drowning each year in England.

The equivalent of an entire classroom of youngsters - 33 in total - is lost with campaigners calling the issue a “national emergency”. In one week alone in May, amid a record breaking heatwave, 19 children and adults were killed in water related incidents.

‌



Front and centre of the campaign is Simon Haycock, whose 16-year-old son Sam drowned in Ulley Reservoir in Rotherham on his last day of school in 2021.

He has been fighting to be heard since the loss of Sam and calls the issue of water safety “a matter of life and death”, adding: “change needs to happen and it needs to happen fast.”

Save Lives for Sam wants the government to launch an urgent public awareness campaign targeting parents and children on TikTok and other social media platforms as well as introduce compulsory water safety lessons in schools.

In addition, the campaign is calling for water companies to introduce correct safety equipment around bodies of water and for the government to appoint a Minister for Water Safety.

‌



The introduction of ‘Sam’s Law’ is also demanded, making it a legal requirement for safety equipment to be installed around high risk areas of water and making damaging the equipment an aggravated criminal offence - currently these offences are deemed minor and carry low penalties.

For property expert Laura, who lives in Surrey with son Rocco, 12 and 11-year-old daughter Tahlia, water safety has always been high on her agenda.

She says: “I started travelling with my children for work when they were three weeks old and they were often around pools and beaches so they had to learn to swim; for me it was non negotiable. I had wonderful people who helped and supported me to do that. When I was a kid the school I attended took us to the leisure centre for lessons too - but not everyone gets those chances.

“Being taught how to swim shouldn’t be seen as a “nice to have” - it’s a fundamental skill, a necessity. That extends to adults. And even if you can swim you still need to be aware of the dangers of open water. We teach people about CPR and life saving skills and that’s great but we need to be encouraging water safety.”

‌



View 4 Images Water safety has always been high on her agenda (Image: Instagram)

Laura, who has her own YouTube channel, Property with Laura Hamilton, admits she was shocked when she discovered some of the data around the number of those losing their lives through drowning.

The World Health Organisation lists it as the third leading cause of death for children aged five to 14.

She adds: “I looked at the statistics and couldn’t believe it - we have to get these numbers down. The campaign is brilliant. Everyone has a duty to be mindful of others. For instance, I was away on holiday with my friend, daughter and her friend. The hotel was on the beach and my mate mentioned that people were getting up early to put their towels on the sunbeds around the pool.

‌



“But she noted those around the pool were adults without children. Surely if you’ve got kids you should be given the priority to actually be on those beds so you can keep an eye on them? It’s such a simple thing, a tiny thing but it could make a difference.”

Laura, who came second in the 2011 series of Dancing on Ice, reveals she spoke to her children in the wake of the French beach tragedy she witnessed: “They were shocked. But it prompted me to ask if they knew what to do if they ran into problems in the sea, say with riptides or currents.

“It's hard because you never want to put your own fears and worries onto children. You still want them to be able to enjoy things, go in the sea or pool, but they have to be equipped with the right information and be aware of the danger.”

Save Lives For Sam is backed by bereaved families as well as The Royal Life Saving Society (RLSSUK), RoSPA (the Royal Society for the Prevention of Accidents, Lee Pitcher MP, the Black Swimming Association (BSA), The National Water Safety Forum, the RNLI, Swim England and The Swimming Alliance.

‌



The Four-time Olympic medallist and TV presenter Becky Adlington OBE has also leant her support as has Triple Olympic champion and RLSS UK Ambassador Tom Dean.

Laura says she’s been both saddened and shocked by some of the stories of people who have lost their lives - adults and children.

She adds: “And for every statistic there’s an individual and a family that’s been changed forever. Just like that lad on the beach. We need information that’s accessible to everybody, better understanding of the risks around water, and a programme of education. That surely can’t be too hard, can it?”

Save Lives for Sam - our demands Together, we are all calling for: The Government to launch an urgent public awareness campaign ahead of the summer holidays which targets parents and children on TikTok and other social media platforms. This should include lifesaving techniques and advice such as avoid diving into the water and information on cold water shock. Water companies and those in control of high risk large water bodies, to ‘do the right thing’ by bringing in the correct safety equipment. Compulsory lessons in schools (ahead of the holidays) on how to survive if you get into difficulty in the water, which should include the Water Safety Code, the RNLI ‘Float to Live’ campaign, and Phone-Float-Throw bystander advice. Put in place ‘Sam’s Law’. We urge the Government to make it law that safety equipment should be installed around high risk large bodies of water and make damaging this safety equipment an aggravated criminal offence to damage or steal this safety equipment. Currently it is already a criminal offence under theft or criminal damage but the penalties are low for these very minor offences. And finally the appointment of a Minister for Water Safety, as they have in Wales and Scotland, as drowning must be accepted as a preventable public health issue.

‌



The Mirror has launched the Save Lives For Sam water safety campaign to tackle the UK's growing drowning crisis. Backed by MPs, Olympic champions, national water safety organisations and bereaved families, the campaign is calling for urgent action to make our waters safer.

That includes compulsory water safety lessons in schools, a nationwide public awareness campaign, better lifesaving equipment at high-risk waterways, the introduction of Sam's Law, and a dedicated Minister for Water Safety. Find out more about the campaign and how you can support it here.
