World.title: Senga Hill residents urged to vote for UPND- Vice President
World.content:
Vice President, Mutale Nalumango, has called on the people of Senga Hill District to vote for the United Party for National Development (UPND) in the August 13 2026 General Elections.

Speaking when she addressed hundreds of people at Mambwe Primary School Ms Nalumango, assured that voting for UPND will ensure continued development in the area.

Mrs Nalumango said Senga Hill District has recorded significant development since the UPND assumed office.

She added that more progress can only be achieved if the people re-elect President Hakainde Hichilema and support UPND candidates.

The Vice President urged citizens to uphold peace before, during and after the elections, saying peace and stability are key to sustaining the country’s development agenda.

She appealed to the electorate to give the UPND another mandate to continue implementing programmes aimed at improving the lives of Zambians.

Mrs Nalumango reaffirmed the government’s commitment to free education, stating that the policy will remain in place to ensure every child has access to quality education.

She added that the government will continue investing in the education sector through the provision of school desks, the School Feeding Programme and the recruitment of more teachers.

Ms Nalumango said the government remains committed to employing more health workers, teachers and other qualified professionals in order to improve service delivery across the country.

The Vice President also encouraged farmers to sell their maize to the Food Reserve Agency (FRA), noting that the government has announced an attractive maize buying price that will enhance household incomes while strengthening national food security.

Ms Nalumango further thanked the people of Senga Hill District for their continued support and further urged them to utilize the increased Constituency Development Fund (CDF) which will accelerate community development projects in the district.

And speaking when she held a meeting with the clergy, Mrs Nalumango called on the church to continue praying for peace and unity in the country.

Speaking on behalf of the clergy, Pastor Wellington Silungwe, encouraged President Hakainde Hichilema and Vice President Mutale Nalumango to remain steadfast in their faith and trust in God regardless of the challenges they face.

Reading from Isaiah 41:10, Pastor Silungwe said God commands his people not to fear or be dismayed because he is always with them.

He said even in the midst of difficulties, trials, or dangerous situations, the President and his Vice should remain courageous, knowing that God will strengthen and protect them.

“Fear should not control lives, God’s presence is greater than any problem or danger that you may encounter,” he said.

Pastor Silungwe further called on the President to continue maintaining a close relationship with God through prayer, obedience, and faith adding that those who remain committed to God will continue to experience his guidance, peace, and strength in every season of life.

While in Senga Hill District the Vice President also held a meeting with Traditional leaders.

Mrs Nalumango has since concluded his 5 days visit of some selected districts in Northern Province with Senga Hill District being the last district to be visited.

World.title: Motorcycle rider attacked and robbed of his motorcycle
World.content:
A 21-year-old motorcycle rider is admitted to Petauke District Hospital after he was allegedly attacked and robbed of his motorcycle by unknown assailant in Petauke District.

Eastern Province Police Commanding Officer, Robertson Mweemba, confirmed the incident to the media saying it occurred on July 31, 2026, around 20:00 hours in Hillside Compound in Chief Kalindawalo’s area.

Mr Mweemba identified the victim as Killion Phiri, 21, of Tasala 10 Compound in Chief Kalindawalo’s area.

He said the matter was reported to Petauke Police Station at about 20:30 hours by the victim, who stated that he was attacked by an unknown man whom he could identify if seen again.

Mr Mweemba explained that the victim, a motorcycle taxi operator, had been hired by the suspect from Petauke Turn-off to Hillside Compound for a fare of K30.

“Upon reaching Hillside Compound, the suspect asked the rider to stop before allegedly striking him on the head several times with a suspected metal bar, “he said.

Mr. Mweemba said the suspect later fled with a black Gatoma motorcycle valued at K25,000. The engine and chassis numbers of the stolen motorcycle have not yet been established.

The Eastern Province Police Chief said the victim sustained multiple cuts to the head but managed to walk to Petauke Police Station, where he reported the matter.

Mr Mweemba said the victim was issued with a police medical report form and rushed to Petauke District Hospital, where he was admitted for treatment.

He added that investigations into the aggravated robbery have been instituted, while efforts to trace the suspect and recover the stolen motorcycle are underway.

World.title: 2026 Kazanga Traditional Ceremony not cancelled-NRE
World.content:
The Nkoya Royal Establishment, (NRE), has dismissed as false reports circulating on social media claiming that the 2026 Kazanga Traditional Ceremony has been cancelled.

NRE Prime Minister, Ntanda Ngwelela, traditionally known as Mwanashihemi said the public should ignore the rumors and treat them as unfounded.

Speaking in an interview to the media in Kaoma today, Mr Ngwelela reaffirmed the Royal Establishment’s commitment to hosting this year’s ceremony as planned.

He said any changes or important developments regarding the event would be communicated through official NRE channels.

“As things stand, the Kazanga Traditional Ceremony will take place as scheduled from 8th to 9th August 2026,” he stated.

The Prime Minister appealed to members of the public, especially those planning to travel to Kaoma, to come and participate in the celebrations.

He expressed concern over the source of the rumors, noting that preparations for the ceremony were progressing smoothly.

The Royal Establishment has since urged the public to rely only on official updates from NRE ahead of the two-day cultural gathering.

Kazanga is the major annual cultural festival of the Nkoya people of Kaoma District in Western Province. The ceremony was revived in 1988 after a period of inactivity.

The event is traditionally a first-fruits harvest ritual and a thanksgiving to God for a bumper harvest.

Historically, Kazanga was also a military occasion used to honour warriors and hunters who distinguished themselves by killing lions and leopards.

World.title: Luangwa set to procure new Mortuary Condensing Unit
World.content:
Luangwa District Health Director, Ikasaya Ikasaya, has thanked the government for the allocation of K153, 000 from the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) to purchase a new mortuary condensing unit at Luangwa District Hospital.

Dr Ikasaya says the current nine body capacity mortuary condensing unit has been malfunctioning for some time despite undergoing many repairs.

Speaking during a meeting at Luangwa District Hospital, the District Health Director, explained that the situation has affected the entire mortuary unit that cannot preserve bodies for a long time.

“The maximum duration the hospital can keep bodies in the mortuary is three days and this has negatively affected the communities around”, he explained.

Dr Ikasaya explained that the process of purchasing a new mortuary condensing unit is at procurement stage.

He said the procurement of the new mortuary condensing unit will ease the preservation of the bodies for longer periods allowing the families ample time to mourn their loved ones.

Meanwhile, Luangwa District Commissioner, Luke Chikani, said the government’s mandate is to ensure that services are brought closer to the people hence its commitment to purchase a new mortuary condensing unit for the district hospital.

Mr Chikani also appreciated the construction of the female and children’s wards at the district hospital which is at 95 percent completion, citing its importance in the provision of quality services to the patients.

“Previously, female adults and children used to share the same ward and this used to deny patient’s their legit privacy but we are happy that this will no longer be the case”, he explained.

The District Commissioner expressed gratitude for the massive development that has taken place in the district.

World.title: Food Security Pack beneficiaries increases in Mpongwe
World.content:
Government has increased the number of beneficiaries under the Wetlands Component of the Food Security Pack (FSP) Programme in Mpongwe District from 700 to 1,100 for the 2026/2027 farming season.

‎

‎Speaking during the official launch of the distribution of farming inputs at Mukulefumo, Mpongwe District Commissioner, Mwitwa Mwambashi, said the increase reflects Government’s commitment to strengthening household food security, reducing poverty and improving the livelihoods of vulnerable but viable farming households through increased agricultural production.

‎

‎Mr Mwambashi said the Ministry of Community Development and Social Services is implementing the Food Security Pack Programme as part of Government’s social protection interventions aimed at promoting inclusive and sustainable community development.

‎

‎He said beneficiaries under the Wetlands Component will receive fertiliser, maize seed, agricultural lime and vegetable seed packs, as well as extension services and training in precision farming and other improved agronomic practices.

‎

‎The District Commissioner disclosed that the Government has also targeted 1,265 households under the Rain-fed Component, bringing the total number of Food Security Pack beneficiaries in Mpongwe District to 2,365 during the 2026/2027 farming season.

‎

‎He urged beneficiaries to utilise the inputs for their intended purpose and refrain from selling them, saying the programme is designed to boost food production, improve household incomes and enhance food security.

‎

‎Mr Mwambashi further noted that Mpongwe’s position as Zambia’s second-largest maize-producing district demonstrates the hard work of its farmers and expressed hope that the Government would consider increasing future allocations to the district.

‎

‎He also commended officers from the Ministry of Community Development and Social Services and other stakeholders for their commitment to the successful implementation of the programme before officially flagging off the distribution of the 2026/2027 Food Security Pack farming inputs.

‎

‎Meanwhile, Mpongwe District Community Development Officer, Humphrey Mununga, said the programme seeks to promote sustainable food production by encouraging communities to engage in farming throughout the year.

‎

‎Mr Mununga said the initiative is intended to help vulnerable but viable households graduate from poverty through increased agricultural productivity.

‎

‎He also appealed to beneficiaries not to sell the farming inputs but to use them productively to improve their livelihoods.

‎

‎And beneficiary, Median Makumbi, thanked the Government for extending the programme to Mukulefumo, saying the farming inputs would help improve crop production and household food security.

‎

‎Ms Makumbi encouraged fellow beneficiaries to make good use of the inputs, increase their yields and ensure they repay the recoveries as required under the programme.

World.title: “I cannot be bought or sold,” says Kaingu, revealing appointment offer she turned down weeks ago
World.content:
Iris Kaingu, the independent parliamentary candidate for Mwandi, has revealed that President Hakainde Hichilema offered her a government appointment weeks ago in exchange for withdrawing from the race, an offer she says she rejected at the time because she refused to be “bought or sold.”

Speaking from Mwandi the morning after the President addressed residents in the constituency, Kaingu said she had regarded the conversation as private until he referred to it publicly. “I thought that our conversation was one that was had in private, that none of what we discussed was going to make it to social media,” she said. “But alas, you, Mr President, mentioned our phone call.”

She said the approach had begun before the President spoke to her directly, when he contacted her father and asked him to persuade her against standing. Her father, she said, told the President he was dealing with a grown woman capable of deciding for herself. The President then called Kaingu directly, roughly two months earlier and after nominations had already closed. She said he guaranteed her a government appointment, citing her standing as a young woman, and a place on the UPND’s national mobilisation and campaign team, if she withdrew her candidature.

Kaingu said she declined both offers then and has not reconsidered since, describing the moment as a test of principle rather than politics. “I am a politician. I seek this office because of servitude,” she said. “I want to be the leader that my people expect me to be, not one person that can be bought or sold.” She admitted the offer had tested her resolve, given the state of the economy, but said her commitment to Mwandi outweighed it. “All these things do not amount to the love I have for the people of Mwandi,” she said. “In this economy, I don’t know that many people who would have said no.”

Her disclosure follows a weekend visit by Hichilema to Mwandi, during which he urged residents to back the UPND’s adopted candidate, Sibeso Sefulo Kakoma, described her independent bid as a sign of greed, and told the crowd that “working alone aikona mani” was unacceptable. Kaingu said his account of the conversation was incomplete. “You should have told the people yesterday what it is you offered me that I said no to,” she said, adding that a one-sided version of events was not good enough for the public to judge fairly.

Kaingu tied her refusal to conditions she said had persisted in Mwandi for years, arguing that no appointment could compensate for what residents were living through. She cited unsafe drinking water, an ungraded 120-kilometre road, women giving birth in oxcarts or at home without maternity care, and the death of a woman in Mavumbu ward during a power cut, when health workers were forced to use a mobile phone torch to locate a vein for treatment. “For as long as the people consume this water, Mr President, I say no to your offer,” she said. “For as long as the children are walking more than twenty kilometres to school, Mr President, I say no.”

She also raised the record of the outgoing Mwandi MP, whom the UPND is fielding again, saying five years in office had left constituents disappointed, and questioned why the President had used his visit to campaign against her rather than account for 2021 pledges she said remained unfulfilled. She disputed the description of Western Province as UPND’s stronghold, noting the province had backed the party even in opposition yet remained, in her words, at the bottom of provincial development rankings. She further pointed out that several sitting UPND figures, including Sunday Chanda, Kampamba Mulenga and Thomas Sipalo, had themselves come from the Patriotic Front, questioning why her own background in the party had been singled out.

On the economy, Kaingu said official indicators bore little relation to household realities. “It doesn’t make economic sense, Mr President, to have a single digit inflation rate, but the cost of living is still very high,” she said, calling for a shift away from what she described as “an economy of spreadsheets.” She also noted that no courtesy call had been paid to the senior chief of the Mulovezi, Mwandi and Sesheke area during the presidential visit, describing it as a departure from custom.

Kaingu thanked independent candidates who had resisted pressure to withdraw, naming Gary Nkombo directly, and appealed to donor organisations to help bring safe water to Mwandi. She closed by telling residents that the coming national vote offered a choice that comes only once every five years, and urged them to use it.

Neither State House nor the UPND had issued a further response to Kaingu’s disclosures at the time of publication.

World.title: Chinsali General Hospital gets staff boost
World.content:
Muchinga Province has marked a significant milestone in its healthcare delivery following the deployment of two Consultant Obstetricians and Gynaecologists to Chinsali General Hospital.

The arrival of Stanley Chungu and Harry Ngosa beefs up the hospital’s specialized medical team, bringing the total number of resident consultants at Chinsali General to three.

Muchinga Province Health Director, David Silweya, says the development increases the total number of specialized OBGYN consultants across Muchinga Province to four, working alongside another specialised consultant based at Chilonga General Mission Hospital in Mpika District.

Dr Silweya hailed the deployment as a turning point for maternal and reproductive healthcare in the region.

He notes that arrival of two OBGYN specialists to the facility fulfills a long-standing commitment to decentralising specialised care.

“This achievement reflects our continued commitment to strengthening local specialist services and expanding access to specialised care right here in the province,” the Provincial Health Director stated.

Dr Silweya charges that the additional of new staff to Chinsali General Hospital which is also a referral center for Muchinga, part of Eastern Province in Chama district, and Northern among others will cut off long distances expectant mothers and families used to incur to access quality OBGYN care services.

” No more long journeys for our mothers and families to access quality OBGYN care,” he said.

Dr Silweya emphasizes that efforts to upgrade the province’s medical capacity will continue adding that the Provincial Health Administration is already pivoting its focus toward recruiting other vital medical specialists to establish a comprehensive care network in Muchinga.

“Securing the services of these two consultants is a big step forward, but our work doesn’t stop here,” he added.

He said the health sector in the province is now channeling the energy into attracting Physicians, Pediatricians, and Surgeons to join the rural health space and help complete a full specialist skill set for the province.

Dr Silweya has since reaffirmed the department’s resolve to improve local health outcomes.

“It’s not an easy undertaking, but it’s one we remain fully dedicated to, for the health and wellbeing of our communities,” he echoed.
